question: Since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why did the authors still prefer Model 1?
expect: premise half false: Model 2 recovers most (99% vs 98%) but its biodiesel has 10x the methanol and 1.5x the glycerol of Model 1 (sec. 3.4, p9)
trap: accepting that Model 2 has fewer impurities
rendered: The authors preferred Model 1 over Model 2 because, although Model 2 recovered the most FAME, it also left more impurities like unconverted methanol and glycerol in the final biodiesel stream. These impurities can be detrimental to the quality and properties of the biodiesel, potentially causing engine corrosion, hazardous emissions, and storage problems. In contrast, Model 1, which uses a reactor-separator arrangement with double-stage distillation, was able to recover a high amount of FAME with fewer impurities, making it the preferred choice.
